A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same time-lagged collective-variable learning project. Despite substantial refocusing, v2 retains v1's alanine results under TBG-CV in Appendix C.6. The text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original alanine dipeptide OPES and steered-MD simulations, quantitative comparisons, sensitivity analyses, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulations and analyses for three proteins, extensive ablations, and supplementary evaluations, alongside retained alanine results.

M1.justification: v1 jointly trains a TBG/EGNN flow backbone and CV encoder using flow matching plus autocorrelation on aligned coordinates. v2 introduces BIOEMU-CV, using a frozen BioEmu diffusion backbone, C-alpha-distance inputs, and a trainable encoder/MLP conditioning pathway optimized by denoising score matching without autocorrelation. The original approach remains as TBG-CV in Appendix C.6; this is substantially more than renaming.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only alanine dipeptide. v2 retains that system and adds DESRES data and explicit-water folding evaluations for Chignolin, Trp-cage, and BBA, substantially expanding molecular and conformational coverage while retaining OPES and transition-path sampling as downstream tasks.

E2.justification: DeepLDA and DeepTDA disappear from the retained alanine comparison: v2 Table 11 preserves DeepTICA, TAE, and VDE from v1 Tables 1–2 but omits both supervised methods. Appendix C.5 additionally evaluates PCA-CVs and TICA-CVs on Trp-cage. These changes alter the comparator families actually tested.

E3.justification: The new protein evaluations introduce 1-microsecond OPES, 500-picosecond SMD, endpoint C-alpha RMSD criteria, PMF MAE, and learned-CV/RMSD mixtures for steering. Appendix C.8 adds approximately 9.8-microsecond OPES. For retained alanine experiments, TAE's stated input changes from aligned coordinates to heavy-atom distances despite identical scores; this establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of time-lagged conditioning, backbone freezing, encoder size, conditioning placement, and SMD without RMSD mixing, plus four-dimensional CVs and longer-simulation convergence analyses. Committor, hydrogen-bond, secondary-structure, and VAMP analyses substantially expand diagnostic coverage. v1's coordinate-representation and autocorrelation ablations are no longer reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report repeated-simulation averages and uncertainty. v2 additionally reports RMSD uncertainty across 16 protein SMD simulations and explicitly labels standard-deviation bands. More substantially, protein OPES estimates exclude one of four runs for Trp-cage and BBA using a specified deviation-from-mean rule, then recompute statistics over three runs (Appendix B.3); v1 uses all four alanine OPES runs.

E6.justification: The retained alanine values are unchanged, including TLC/TBG-CV's free-energy difference of 9.83 ± 1.15 and THP of 60.93%, while the DeepLDA/DeepTDA rows disappear. v2 adds extensive protein results, including BIOEMU-CV THPs of 100.0%, 31.2%, and 93.8% under RMSD-assisted steering. These are new-condition results, not gains over v1. Added ablations also show mixed outcomes: removing time lag improves PMF MAE but reduces THP in Table 13.

T1.justification: The mathematical specification changes from explicit flow-matching and autocorrelation losses in v1 to a conditional denoising-score objective in v2 Equation 1, with a no-lag variant in Appendix D.1. v2 also defines thresholded PMF MAE. These are limited changes to formal specifications; neither version develops theorems, proofs, or formal performance guarantees.

C1.justification: v1 presents TLC as a generative CV-learning framework validated on alanine dipeptide. v2 redefines the principal contribution as lightweight extraction of CVs from frozen BioEmu and adds a claimed systematic benchmark on proteins beyond alanine. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion consequently change the method's novelty claim and empirical scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting CVs to protein contacts, committors, and secondary structures, and explains why apparent OPES convergence or high VAMP scores can be misleading. Appendix D.3 motivates RMSD assistance through failures of unassisted SMD, although force constants also differ. These substantially expand applicability and failure discussions beyond v1's alanine-specific interpretations and autocorrelation tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 adds DESRES sampling instructions, training/validation proportions, activation, dropout and early-stopping settings, software versions, solvation procedures, hardware, and runtime information in Appendices A–B. Its code link changes from the TLC repository to an anonymous BIOEMU-CV resource. Some earlier details disappear from the condensed alanine account, including the explicit 1000-femtosecond training lag; the protein training lag also remains numerically unspecified.

R1.justification: The central positioning shifts from TBG and continuous normalizing flows to adapting a pretrained molecular foundation model. v2 adds BioEmu, T2I-Adapter, AlphaFold, DESRES, committor, and protein-analysis references, and emphasizes scalability and the absence of systematic protein benchmarks. TBG remains cited for the appendix variant, while much of v1's flow-matching background and associated references disappears.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. OPES now precedes SMD, interpretability and state discrimination receive dedicated sections, and the original central alanine study is condensed into Appendix C.6. The appendices are reorganized, with new reproducibility and disclosure statements.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation, redraws the method overview around BioEmu, and introduces extensive protein trajectory, TICA, sensitivity, and secondary-structure displays. The original alanine OPES and SMD tables are merged into Table 11, and pathway panels are reconfigured in Figure 16. Several original alanine diagnostic plots disappear.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical conclusions rest on one small molecule. v2 substantially strengthens that foundation through three protein systems, comparisons against long DESRES trajectories, structural validation, and controls examining conditioning, freezing, and failure modes. These additions make applicability and design choices much more assessable. RMSD-assisted SMD, OPES outlier filtering, mixed ablation outcomes, and missing training details limit the strength of performance claims, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support and diagnostic transparency.
